items.title: bob requesting alice's order gets 404 with no order data
covers: Steps to Reproduce: step 3
Expected: step 3 answers 404 with no order data
Actual: 200 with alice's shipping address, items and payment description
items.reason: This is the reported defect: a shopper could read another shopper's order (address, items, payment description). If it regresses, any signed-in user can leak every other user's personal data by walking order numbers. It runs on the test stack because the order must really exist and belong to alice, which the functional host cannot save.

items.title: bob requesting order 999999 gets 404 with no body
covers: Steps to Reproduce: step 4, second bullet
Expected: the answer bob gets in step 4 for an order that does not exist
items.reason: The story uses the missing-order answer as the reference that step 3 must match; this case pins that reference so the fix does not change it (for example into a 400 or a problem body). It runs on the test stack next to TC-BUG-47-01 so both answers come from the same deployed API.

items.title: bob's answer for alice's order is identical to his answer for a missing order
covers: Expected: the same answer bob gets in step 4 for an order that does not exist, so he cannot tell that the order exists
items.reason: The story requires more than a refusal: the refusal must not reveal that the order exists (no 403, no different body or headers). A fix that answered 403, or a 404 with a different body, would pass TC-BUG-47-01's status check in spirit but still leak existence; this case compares the two answers directly.

items.title: alice requesting her own order still gets 200 with the order
covers: Steps to Reproduce: step 4, first bullet
Expected: alice still gets her own order (200), as today
items.reason: The fix filters orders by owner; a wrong filter (for example comparing against the wrong claim) would hide every order from its owner too. This case proves the owner still gets the full order, on the test stack where the order really exists.

items.title: alice requesting bob's order gets 404 with no order data
covers: Bug Report: any signed-in shopper who asks for an order by its number gets that order
items.reason: The bug report says "any signed-in shopper", so the rule must hold in both directions, not only for bob looking at alice's order. This guards against a fix that only works for one seeded user or one order.

items.title: bob requesting his own order still gets 200 with the order
covers: Expected: the owner still gets the order (200), as today
items.reason: Pairs with TC-BUG-47-05: it shows the 404 alice gets for `B` is because of ownership, not because `B` is unreadable, and that a second owner still reads his own order.

items.title: alice's order list still lists only her orders, including A
covers: Expected: GET /api/orders (the signed-in shopper's list) works exactly as today
items.reason: The story requires the list endpoint to be unchanged. It shares the query class with the fixed endpoint, so a regression there would hide orders from their owner or mix in others'.

items.title: bob's order list does not contain alice's order
covers: Expected: GET /api/orders (the signed-in shopper's list) works exactly as today
items.reason: The list must keep returning only the caller's orders for every user; this checks the other side of TC-BUG-47-07 so the list cannot become another way to see alice's order number.

subject: BUG-47
reason: Council (testPlan, blockOn any, pass 9/10): not passed; opus 9/10, sol 7/10; 4 finding(s) stand, 1 note(s).

items.reason: Delete this standalone case. TC-BUG-47-03 already exercises the missing-order error path, while TC-BUG-47-01 and TC-BUG-47-03 retain every assertion this case adds.
Delete this mirrored ownership case. Neither shopper has a distinct role or permission in the plan, so reversing their names introduces no additional authorization branch.
Delete this second owner-access case. It changes only the seeded user and order number; TC-BUG-47-04 preserves the owner's 200 response and order-content coverage.
Delete this mirrored list case. TC-BUG-47-07 already verifies 200, the JSON array, inclusion of the caller's order and exclusion of another shopper's order.

The shared setup body for POST /api/orders lists only userId, card type, card number, address and one item. CreateOrderCommandValidator also requires CardHolderName, a future CardExpiration and a 3-digit CardSecurityNumber, so a test built literally from the plan gets 400 and places no order A or B. Name the full body (userName, buyer, cardHolderName, cardExpiration e.g. 2030-12-31T00:00:00Z, cardSecurityNumber '123', items with productId/productName/unitPrice/quantity) or point to the order() body in e2e/teststack/bug-30.spec.ts:49-63.
